title: Synthesizers
subtitle: How a sound is built
summary: Helmholtz spent the 1860s working out why a clarinet and a flute sound different on the same note, and that is where this course begins. A synthesizer sits beside every lesson, so each idea, from the filter and the envelope to FM and echo, is something you hear and then make. The later lessons follow one real instrument, Arturia's MicroFreak, and the last builds five sounds from a blank patch. PatchMatch, a game of copying sounds by ear, is there too.

release.note: Every lesson revised after a student read-through: terms defined where they first appear, clearer tasks for the live synth, and numbers checked against the synth itself.
